title: 4.6. Defining Regionalism and Regional Integration 🗺️
content: 📌 እንኳን ደህና መጣችሁ ውድ የኢትዮፍሬሽ ተማሪዎቻችን! የክፍል አራት (Chapter 4) ሁለተኛውን ክፍል አብረን አንቀጥላለን! 👋✨ Basic Definitions: • Region: A limited number of states linked together by geographical proximity and mutual interdependence (Nye, 1968). • Regionalism: Sustained political and/or economic cooperation among three or more countries for mutual gains (Allagappa, 1994) [cite: Regionalism consequently refers to intensifying political and/or economic processes of cooperation among states and other actors in particular geographic regions... Regionalism normally presents the sustained cooperation (either formal or informal) among governments, non-governmental organizations, or the private sectors in three or more countries for mutual gains]. - 'From Below': Driven by market forces, companies, and population movements. - 'From Above': Driven by state political efforts to form common policies. Three Levels of Region (Buzan et al., 1998): 1. Region: Spatially coherent territory composed of two or more states. 2. Sub-region: Part of a region involving some (not all) states or transnational mix. 3. Micro-region: Subunit level within the internal boundaries of a single state. 👉 Example: በምስራቅ አፍሪካ የሚገኙ ሀገራት (እንደ ኢትዮጵያ፣ ኬንያ፣ ኡጋንዳ) በጂኦግራፊ መቃረባቸው ብቻ ሳይሆን በመካከላቸው ባለው ኢኮኖሚያዊና ፖለቲካዊ ቁርኝት ምክንያት ክልላዊ ማህበር (እንደ IGAD) ይመሰርታሉ። 💡 Exam Focus: Spatial concept is essential, but WITHOUT "regionness" (regional awareness), proximity alone is not enough! [cite: These literatures led to a conclusion that a spatial concept is the essence of regionalism... However, without regionness or regional awareness the proximity of countries in the given regions cannot be referred to as a key driving force to regionalize with intimate neighboring countries.]

title: Regionalization vs. Regionalism & Theory Context 🤝
content: 📌 Key Conceptual Distinctions: • Regionalization: - The growth of societal integration and undirected social/economic interactions within a region. - A continuing dynamic process forming geopolitical units and pluralistic security communities. • Regionalism: - The deliberate proneness of governments and peoples to pool material/nonmaterial resources in formal arrangements. - Actors share fundamental values and build networks across economic, cultural, and military spheres. Eurocentric Theoretical Bias: • Regionalism theories were overwhelmingly developed based on the successful European context [cite: The occurrences of regionalism have mushroomed across all parts of the world. In contrast, the theories to explain these developments are limited... Most of the theories have been developed under the dominant European contexts. This is due largely to the location of regionalism and its successful story has been in the specific context of Europe.]. • Traditional Eurocentric theories are often ill-suited for non-Western regions like Southeast Asia or Africa. 😅 Quick Joke: Trying to apply early European regional integration theories directly to developing nations is like trying to install a Windows 11 update on a 1990s Nokia phone—it just wasn't built for that architecture! 👉ሬጂዮናላይዜሽን በራሱ የሚከናወን የህብረተሰብ ትስስር ሲሆን፣ ሬጂዮናሊዝም ደግሞ በህግና በተቋም የታገዘ የመንግስታት ፈቃደኝነት ነው።

title: 4.6.1. Old Regionalism: European Integration 🇪🇺
content: 📌 Old Regionalism: Origin & European Model • Historical Emergence: Predominantly a post-WWII phenomenon (late 1940s) aimed at preventing war. • Core Motivation: Nation-states were viewed as the problem (due to deadly nationalism), and integration was the solution for peace and stability [cite: In contrast to earlier discussions that centered on mercantilism and competing alliances, post-War scholars usually viewed the (Westphalian) nation-state as the problem rather than the solution, and the purpose of regional integration was to achieve and consolidate peace and stability.]. Key Milestones in Europe: 1. ECSC (1951): European Coal and Steel Community launched to reconcile France and Germany [cite: Immediately after the Second World War, there was a lot of discussion about European regionalism, not least about reconstruction and reconciliation between France and Germany. A series of initiatives were launched, which resulted in the European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) in 1951.]. 2. Treaty of Rome (1958): Integrated European Economic Community (EEC) and EURATOM into the European Communities (EC). 👉Example: በሁለተኛው የዓለም ጦርነት ተፋላሚ የነበሩት ፈረንሳይና ጀርመን የድንጋይ ክስልና ብረት ሀብታቸውን በአንድነት በማስተዳደር ለዘላቂ ሰላም መያዣ አደረጉ። 💡 Exam Hint: Old Regionalism in Europe prioritized political unification and peace through incremental economic integration! [cite: In contrast to earlier discussions that centered on mercantilism and competing alliances, post-War scholars usually viewed the (Westphalian) nation-state as the problem rather than the solution, and the purpose of regional integration was to achieve and consolidate peace and stability.]

title: Old Regionalism in the Developing World: Latin America 🌎
content: 📌 Old Regionalism in Developing Regions: Latin America • Contrast with Europe: Focused on anti-colonialism, nation-building, state-led industrialization, and economic development rather than political unification or peace [cite: As previously indicated, the discussion about regionalism in the developing world was closely linked to colonialism/anti-colonialism and the quest to facilitate economic development in the newly independent nation-states... keywords here were development, state promoted industrialization and nation-building]. • Structuralist School: Pioneered by Raul Prebisch, Gunnar Myrdal, and Arthur Lewis via UN-ECLA [cite: Many of the discussions about regionalism in the developing world were heavily influenced by the structuralist tradition of economic development, pioneered by Gunnar Myrdal, Arthur Lewis, and Raúl Prebisch... Encouraged by the United Nations Economic Commission for Latin America (ECLA) and its dynamic Executive Secretary, Raúl Prebisch]. • Import-Substitution Industrialization (ISI): - Expanding economic space to substitute imports regionally when national markets became too small. - Combining intra-regional trade liberalization with regional protectionism. • Major Initiative: Latin American Free Trade Association (LAFTA, 1960). • Outcome: Failed to make a lasting economic impact due to internal conflicts and military dictatorships [cite: However, in spite of some early progress... the old regionalism in Latin America made little economic impact and was never implemented on a larger scale. Regionalization in Latin America during 1960s and 1970s did not materialized because of conflict and military dictatorship.]. 👉በላቲን አሜሪካ የነበረው የድሮ ሬጂዮናሊዝም አላማ የውጭ እቃዎችን በሀገር ውስጥ ምርት መተካት (Import Substitution) እና ከምዕራባውያን ጥገኝነት መውጣት ነበር።

title: Old Regionalism in Africa 🌍⛏️
content: 📌 Old Regionalism Framework in Africa: • Core Purpose: Resisting colonial/post-colonial influence, promoting protectionism, and pursuing import substitution. • Ideological Debates: Shaped by the Casablanca Group (Federalist/Pan-African) vs. Monrovia Group (Gradualist/State-centric). • Founding Frameworks: Embodied in OAU/AU principles, the Lagos Plan of Action (1980), and the Abuja Treaty (1991) [cite: The major ideological influence on regional cooperation and integration, however, is embodied in the founding principles of OAU and later AU such as Lagos Plan of Action (1980) and the Abuja treaty (1991).]. Early State-Led Organizations in Africa: • CFA: Community of French Africa. • EAC: East African Community. • SACU: Southern African Customs Union. • SADCC: Southern Africa Development Coordination Conference (predecessor of SADC, created specifically to counter Apartheid South Africa's economic dominance). 👉Example: SADCC የተመሠረተው በወቅቱ ደቡብ አፍሪካ ውስጥ በነበረው የአፓርታይድ ስርዓት ላይ ያለን ኢኮኖሚያዊ ጥገኝነት ለመቀነስና የመከላከል አቅምን ለማጠናከር ነበር። 💡 Exam Focus: SADCC was formed specifically to counter Apartheid influence and external dependency!

title: 4.6.2. The New Regionalism (1980s–Present) 🚀📈
content: 📌 Emergence of New Regionalism: Triggered by the Single European Act (1985), the falling Berlin Wall, and post-Cold War structural changes [cite: The prospects of the fall of the Berlin Wall together with the 1985 White Paper on the internal market and the Single European Act resulted in a new dynamic process of European integration. This was also the start of what has often been referred to as ‘new regionalism’ on a global scale.]. Key Characteristics of New Regionalism: 1. Explosive Growth: Spectacular increase in regional trade agreements globally. 2. Open Regionalism: Outward-oriented and less protectionist compared to the old regionalism. 3. Anti-Hegemonic & Bottom-Up: Emerges internally from within regions rather than controlled by Cold War superpowers. 4. Multi-Dimensional: Broadened beyond mere trade or military security to cover environment, human rights, and social policy. 5. Pluralistic Actors: Active involvement of MNCs, private business sectors, and civil society alongside states. 👉አዲሱ ሬጂዮናሊዝም በንግድ ላይ ብቻ የተወሰነ ሳይሆን መንግስታዊ ያልሆኑ ድርጅቶችና የግል ባለሀብቶች የሚሳተፉበት ሁለገብ ትስስር ነው!

title: Old Regionalism vs. New Regionalism: Detailed Comparison 📊
content: 📌 Summary Table (Söderbaum, 2015): | Feature | Old Regionalism (1950s–1970s) | New Regionalism (1980s–Present) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | World Order Context | Bipolar / Cold War Era | Post-Cold War / Multipolar System | | Governance Focus | Taming nationalism (Europe) / Advancing nationalism (South) | Resisting, taming, or advancing globalization | | Actors & Forms | State-centric, hard/formal, sector-specific | Multi-sectoral, state vs non-state, soft/informal | | Ontology & Boundaries| Clear territorial boundaries & rigid institutions | Ontological confusion, fluid boundaries, networks | | Epistemology | Positivism, Rationalism, Materialism | Constructivism, Critical Theory, Focus on Identities | | Methodology | Europe-focused rigid comparisons | Global comparative studies, IR dialogue | 💡 Exam Focus: Expect direct table comparison questions on exam papers! Remember: Old = Bipolar & State-centric; New = Multipolar & Pluralistic!

title: Two Waves of Regionalism: Historical Timeline 🌊🗓️
content: 📌 First Wave Organizations (1950s–1970s): • Europe/Soviet Bloc: NATO (1949), ECSC (1952), Warsaw Pact (1955), EEC (1958), COMECON (1948). • Asia: SEATO (1954), CENTO (1950s), ASEAN (1967). • Latin America: OAS (1948), CACM (1961), Andean Community (1969), CARICOM (1973), LAFTA (1969). • Middle East & Africa: Arab League (1945), OAU (1964). Second Wave Organizations (1980s–1990s+): • Europe: European Union (EU, 1992), CIS (1991). • Asia-Pacific: APEC (1989), ARF (1994). • Americas: MERCOSUR (1991), NAFTA (1993). • Africa: ECOWAS (1975), SADC (1992), COMESA (1994), African Union (AU, 2002). --- ❤️ ውድ የኢትዮፍሬሽ ተማሪዎቻችን! የምዕራፍ 4 ሁለተኛውን ክፍል እዚህ ላይ አጠናቅቀናል። በርቱ! 🙏🙏🙏
